result.title: Task Vectors Can Be Linearly Decomposed into Interpretable and Controllable Components
result.summary: Task Vectors (TVs) provide a compact way to steer large language models, but they are typically treated as atomized directions merely extracted from hidden states, leaving their internal functional structure poorly understood. Motivated by prior work that decomposes in-context learning into Task Recognition (TR) and Task Learning (TL), we ask whether a single TV can likewise be decomposed into functionally meaningful components. We formulate a TR/TL-based decomposition from candidate-label unembeddings, separating each TV into TR, TL, and residual components, and try to optimize the TR and TL coefficients using Bayesian optimization for more effective intervention. We evaluate this formulation across multiple model families, classification tasks, and both instruction- and demonstration-based TVs. Across these settings, TR/TL-based optimization identifies intervention directions that outperform the original TVs. Although optimization over random directions can also improve performance, TR/TL-based search yields more reliable gains, particularly for instruction-based TVs. Moreover, isolated interventions on the decomposed components produce distinct logit-level effects that are consistent with their intended functional roles. Together, these results suggest that TVs are not monolithic steering directions, but can be decomposed into functionally meaningful components that support both interpretation and control.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 Task Vector 的内部功能结构，借助候选标签 unembedding 将单个 TV 分解为任务识别（TR）、任务学习（TL）与残差成分，并用 Bayesian optimization 优化 TR/TL 系数做干预，在多种模型与分类任务上验证分解后的方向更有效且具有可解释的 logit 效应。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 steering 工作，但「把单一隐向量分解为功能子成分并优化干预系数」的思路可供核查是否能用于分离 latent 推理状态中的任务识别与推理更新、或用于多 latent 假设的筛选与控制；原文未涉及视觉证据或推理期状态生成。
